title: Stage 1 adaptive send-path policy contract
purpose: Define the common force, observe, shadow, latch, safety, evidence, and rollback contract for the four Stage 1 adaptive-runtime send-path axes without authorizing active production selection.
scope: This specification covers application_send_turn_planning, application_send_batch_formation, queued_send_burst_budget, and oversized_write_admission_quantum as independently forceable and observable connection-local axes. One counterfactual treatment may vary one axis while every adjacent applied axis remains legacy_current. It does not define a policy winner, production threshold, active_internal behavior, online learning, or a large campaign.
context: The send-turn axis already has a behavior-neutral force and shadow foundation, while batch formation, queued-send burst budget, and oversized-write admission retain existing legal mechanisms that need named policy seams. Unified connection-epoch evidence must represent every implemented axis even when only one treatment varies, and separate construction, packet-plan, actor-turn, and logical-write records must remain independently attributable through deterministic joins.
open_questions: Which bounded pre-decision observation subset will remain useful across three or more independent host fingerprints without encoding workload identity?
Which Stage 1 axes will have evidence strong enough to justify a later one-axis active_internal review after Stage 2 foundations are complete?

requirements.title: Retain one unified Stage 1 epoch and exact decision joins
requirements.statement: Every bounded Stage 1 connection epoch MUST retain exactly one versioned record for application_send_turn_planning, application_send_batch_formation, queued_send_burst_budget, and oversized_write_admission_quantum in canonical order; permit at most one forced treatment; keep every unforced adjacent applied value at legacy_current; preserve forced, shadow, selected, applied, reason, safety, latch, fallback, outcome, run, binary, host, workload, and source provenance; and validate separate construction or operation records through the deterministic campaign, run, cell, sample, connection, epoch, axis, and decision-sequence join without admitting analysis-only workload identity into production controller inputs.
notes: Scenario, payload, requested concurrency, peer, URL, and application identity remain analysis-only provenance.
Separate decision artifacts retain their own source path and checksum; they are not relabeled as the unified epoch source.

requirements.title: Select a safe application-send batch at the packet-plan boundary
requirements.statement: The application_send_batch_formation axis MUST select one value from the closed legacy_current and single_eligible set at the packet-plan boundary, latch that value for exactly one packet plan, expose forced, observe-only, shadow, missing, stale, saturated, contradictory, out-of-domain, safety-override, outcome, replay, and force-legacy evidence, and restrict every proposal to a legal prefix already bounded by payload, priority, same-stream ordering, FIN, ownership, recovery, congestion, pacing, anti-amplification, flow-control, packet, queue, buffer, cancellation, disposal, lifecycle, and terminal-state authority.
notes: single_eligible means the first already-eligible write only; it does not choose a different stream, bypass eligibility, or increase a legal payload budget.
Shadow recommendation cannot alter the packet plan.

requirements.title: Lower the queued-send burst cap without bypassing transport authority
requirements.statement: The queued_send_burst_budget axis MUST select one value from the closed legacy_current and single_datagram set at the application-send actor-turn boundary, latch that value for exactly one actor turn, expose forced, observe-only, shadow, validity, safety, outcome, replay, and force-legacy evidence, and apply its proposal only as a lower bound beneath congestion, pacing, anti-amplification, handshake, recovery, packet, endpoint, retransmission, flow-control, queue, buffer, cancellation, disposal, lifecycle, and terminal-state limits.
notes: The existing established and pre-handshake caps remain the legacy_current mechanism.
Forced selection never increases a legal datagram budget.

requirements.title: Latch oversized-write admission for one logical write
requirements.statement: The oversized_write_admission_quantum axis MUST select one value from the closed legacy_current, single_fragment, and bounded_multi_fragment set at logical-write admission, retain the resolved quantum immutably for the entire logical write, expose forced, observe-only, shadow, validity, safety, outcome, replay, and force-legacy evidence, and preserve byte identity, byte order, stream ordering, FIN, ownership, continuation, recovery, congestion, pacing, anti-amplification, flow-control, packet, queue, buffer, cancellation, disposal, lifecycle, terminal-state, and exactly-once completion authority.
notes: The retained c16-c24 two-fragment selector remains the legacy_current mechanism until counterfactual evidence supports a reviewed rule proposal.
A later epoch cannot change the latch for an admitted logical write.
